Reversa migration · visual verification

Oracle vs Rebuild

Every screen below is served twice: once by a live WordPress 7.2-alpha-63330 instance, and once by the Rails rebuild reading the same content out of PostgreSQL. The WordPress instance is not a testing aid — with no live deployment, it is the project's only executable definition of the 363 migrated rules. Wave 0 is complete and its gate passes. The rebuild renders the real theme through a server-side block renderer, and all twenty-five screens are byte-identical to the oracle through the parity harness — five consecutive clean runs on a corpus proven reproducible across full oracle rebuilds. What that does not cover is stated at the end.

What these pictures do not show

Read this before drawing conclusions from the pairs above.

All twenty-five match, and what that does and does not mean

screen_modernization_decision.md classes the eighteen web.* screens as literal — byte-comparable against a golden file. All eighteen now are, and so are the seven syndication surfaces. parity_specs.md defines the gate as zero unexplained divergence across five consecutive runs on a reproducible corpus; that held.

"Byte-identical through the harness" has a precise meaning. The normalizer masks per-request nonces, autoincrement ids, the UUID guid (T-07, by design), timestamps, the site host — and, declared in the manifest, it sorts class-attribute tokens. So class order (BR-MIGRATE-201) is invisible here on purpose and is asserted by unit specs instead. Two of those are currently pending on a documented gap: block style variation rulesets (class-wp-theme-json.php:3834, step 6) are not ported, so block-level variations get neither their instance class nor their CSS. No golden screen exercises it. pending fails the build if it starts passing, so it cannot close silently.

web.attachment is a redirect, and that is the correct answer

On a default WordPress 7.2 install wp_attachment_pages_enabled is '0' and canonical.php:553 301-redirects every attachment URL to the file. The golden is that redirect; the rebuild now issues the same one. It was listed among the eighteen literal screens as a rendered page, which the running software contradicts — a screen-inventory discrepancy that feeds deferred item D-7.

Byte-identical HTML is not a working page

web.not_found_404 reached byte parity while rendering visibly broken: the externally-linked block stylesheet, the theme's two variable fonts and the navigation view script module all 404'd, because the rebuild served none of the assets its own markup references. The harness compares HTML and cannot see that.

bin/rails assets:sync now copies them, derived from what the goldens actually reference so the list cannot drift from what the pages ask for. It also exposed a corpus defect: the seeder recorded _wp_attachment_metadata['sizes'] without writing the files, so every srcset pointed at a 404 — in both systems equally, which is exactly why no parity check caught it.

Four rules that only a byte diff would find

Block stylesheets are emitted in post-order. A container enqueues its stylesheet only after its children have rendered, so the document order is children-before-parents — site-title → page-list → navigation → group, not the order blocks are met on the way down. That governs 39% of a page's bytes.

A block that renders to nothing contributes no stylesheet. class-wp-block.php:757, new in WordPress 6.9: assets are enqueued unconditionally and then dequeued again if the content trims to empty. The footer pattern carries an unconditional <!-- wp:site-logo /-->, no logo is set, and no golden contains wp-block-site-logo-inline-css.

Script modules are enqueued from render callbacks, not declared in block.json — core/navigation asks for its view module only when the menu is interactive. And the import map carries the dependencies of what rendered, never the modules themselves, because an enqueued module gets a real <script> tag instead.

An earlier diff caught a real bug, which is the argument for looking

The rebuild was rendering its own site title as Reversa Oracle &quot;7.2&quot; — entities visible on screen. WordPress runs sanitize_option() on every option write (BR-MIGRATE-014), so blogname is already HTML-escaped at rest; the oracle's own row literally contains &quot;. WordPress prints it raw. Rails escaped it a second time.

Fixed as a named exception for the two option names WordPress escapes on write, not a blanket raw — the practical stand-in for the SafeHtml value object until that type is wired through the surfaces. No test caught this; a picture did.

The pictures are reproducible; that took work

Three separate sources of drift had to be removed before two captures of the same corpus agreed: wp_install() stamps its seed content with the real clock, every seeded post shared one date and WordPress orders archives by date with no tiebreak, and the embed screen carries a per-request token. bin/parity determinism 5 now rebuilds the oracle from scratch five times and gets byte-identical captures.

That is a precondition, not a nicety: the parity gate is defined as five consecutive clean runs, which is unmeetable if the corpus moves underneath it.

What the left pane proves that the right one cannot

The oracle is seeded adversarially on purpose — all 16 post types, a three-deep category tree, four-level comment threads, drafts carrying 0000-00-00 00:00:00, serialized metadata, emoji and Windows paths full of backslashes. An oracle seeded with three posts proves very little.

That corpus round-trips into PostgreSQL through Active Record with an empty dead-letter queue and all 13 quality validations green, including the two that are easiest to get backwards: byte-identical text (which is what catches an accidental unslashing pass) and terms counted against wp_term_taxonomy rather than wp_terms.

Captured with Playwright at 1180×820, both systems running locally, same corpus, same moment. Screens are ordered as they appear in spec/parity/corpus/requests.yml — the same file the parity harness reads, so the report and the harness cannot drift apart.

Waves 3–5 are not started: there is no write path, no admin console and no editor. Every screen here was brought to parity by fixing causes the byte diff surfaced and the rule text did not — post-order stylesheet enqueueing, the empty-render dequeue, the sticky-post id that pointed at the wrong record — which is the argument for the oracle existing at all.
